title: Ridgeline Pro Credit Disputes Desk Rules — The Resolution Clock of an Invoice Dispute
content:
The resolution clock of an invoice dispute on a Ridgeline Pro Credit account is counted in calendar days to the date the dispute request was approved. Its starting day depends on how soon the dispute was filed after the invoice date and on how long the account has been open.

## Rule

1. When the dispute was filed no more than **30** days after the invoice date and the account has been open at least **60** whole months, the clock runs from the invoice date to the approval date.
2. When the dispute was filed no more than **30** days after the invoice date and the account has been open less than **60** whole months, the clock runs from the day after the filing date to the approval date.
3. When the dispute was filed later than **30** days after the invoice date, the clock runs from the filing date to the approval date.

## Counting conventions

- **Filing lag**: calendar days from the invoice date (day 0) to the date the dispute request was filed. Day 30 is within "no more than 30 days"; day 31 is later.
- **Clock days**: calendar days from the clock's starting day (day 0) to the approval date. A clock that starts on the day after the filing date therefore counts one day fewer than a clock starting on the filing date.
- **Account age**: whole calendar months from the account's opening date to the date the dispute credit is posted. 60 whole months meets "at least 60"; 59 does not.
- The invoice date is that of the disputed invoice line; the filing date and the approval date are those of the approved invoice dispute request.

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates)

Invoice dated 1 March; dispute filed 21 March (filing lag 20 days); request approved 5 May.

| Account age at posting | Starting day | Clock days to 5 May |
|---|---|---|
| 72 whole months | 1 March (invoice date) | 65 |
| 40 whole months | 22 March (day after filing) | 44 |

Same invoice; dispute filed 10 April (filing lag 40 days); approved 5 May: the clock runs from 10 April and counts 25 days, whatever the account's age.
